# Signed-account known answers

These numbers were calculated directly from cash flows, not generated by the
oracle. Decimal strings are exact. `fill` is a manual signed quantity change;
`mark` changes quoted prices; `borrow` charges prior-close short value for the
specified nonnegative whole number of elapsed calendar days before any next-open
fill. Separate tests check atomic refusal of unaffordable fills. A fill itself
marks that symbol at its fill price. Costs are cumulative. Omitted positions
are flat.

The account is deliberately **unfunded and non-broker-feasible** after an
exogenous loss or financing charge makes free cash negative. It is not a cash
loan facility. Negative balances and even negative equity remain visible;
there are no collateral calls, haircuts, margin interest, or automatic sales.
New manual fills must leave free cash nonnegative, including the complete fee.
The runtime will need its own partial-order planner; these fixtures do not
implement one. No Qlib engine or adapter is asserted to pass this harness.

In `short_partial.json`, selling 10 at 10 leaves the 100 proceeds restricted;
covering five releases 50 of those original proceeds even though the cover
costs 40. In `reversals.json`, a 10-share short covered at 12 releases its
original 100, then the remaining five shares open long at 12. The reverse
case closes five longs at 12, then restricts 36 from three new shorts.

In `pooled_short_proceeds.json`, the same short is opened at 10 and 20. Its
restricted pool is 40 + 120 = 160 for 10 shares, so covering five releases
80, independent of the later marks or the 15 cover price.

`weekend_and_deficit.json` uses 36,500 short shares at 1: the Friday close
value is 36,500, and 36,500 × 0.004 × 3 / 365 = 1.2. The second case uses
a one-year charge of 10,000 × 0.004 = 40 after an adverse mark.
